title: What If a Country Abolished Its Army? Costa Rica Did in 1948

scenes.text: What if a country simply abolished its army? One did, and it still has no army today.
December 1, 1948. Costa Rica's leader, Jose Figueres, had just won a five-week civil war. He tore down a wall of the army's main barracks.
In 1949 the constitution made it law: the army as a permanent institution is abolished. The barracks became the National Museum.
The military budget went to schools and hospitals. By 2009, 6.3 percent of the economy went to education and 7 percent to health.
In 1955 it was invaded from Nicaragua anyway. A civil guard and volunteers held out, and diplomacy did the rest.
Today: free healthcare, free university, and Panama copied the idea in 1990. The weapon that worked was a budget.

description:
What if a country abolished its army? Costa Rica did on December 1, 1948, when Jose Figueres symbolically tore down a wall of the Bellavista barracks; the 1949 constitution bans a permanent army and the barracks are now the National Museum.
Military spending was redirected to education and health, funding free schooling and universal healthcare, and Panama followed in 1990.
